name: Heber (a Kenite, the husband of Jael)
title: The Kenite who separated from his tribe
summary: Heber was a Kenite descended from Hobab, Moses' father-in-law. He separated from the other Kenites and settled near Kedesh in Naphtali. He is best known as the husband of Jael, who killed the Canaanite commander Sisera.

keyEvents.title: Heber's descent from Hobab
keyEvents.description: Heber descended from Hobab, Moses' father-in-law, and was thus a Kenite with ties to the people of Israel.

keyEvents.title: Separated from the Kenites
keyEvents.description: Heber left the other Kenites and moved northward, which was unusual since the Kenites usually stayed together.

keyEvents.title: Encamped near Kedesh
keyEvents.description: Heber pitched his tent by Elon-bezaanannim near Kedesh in the territory of Naphtali, which was strategically located.

keyEvents.title: Peace with Jabin
keyEvents.description: There was peace between Heber the Kenite and King Jabin of Hazor, so that Sisera sought refuge with his family.
